style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The prayer of an old man, and it is stitched almost entirely out of other psalms -- its first three verses are Psalm 31's, and lines from 22, 35, 40 and others turn up throughout. That is the point: a man who has been praying Scripture his whole life prays it again at the end, and the words are worn smooth. His argument is his biography. You have been my confidence from my youth; I have leaned on You from birth; You took me from my mother's body; You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I keep telling Your wonders. So the request is simply that the pattern hold: do not throw me away at the time of old age, do not abandon me when my strength gives out -- because his enemies have read the gray hair as evidence and are saying God has left him, chase him down, no one will rescue him. Against that he sets the one thing age has actually given him, a longer list of things to praise for, and one job left to do: until I have declared Your arm to the next generation, Your power to everyone still to come. Then a promise no old man could make on his own -- You will revive me again, and bring me up again from the depths of the earth -- and the psalm ends with an old voice, a lyre, and lips shouting.

1.text: In You, O LORD, I have sheltered; never let me be put to shame.
1.amp: In You, O LORD [YHWH], do I put my trust [chasah -- take refuge]: let me never [olam] be put to confusion [bosh].
1.notes: bekha YHWH chasiti al-eboshah le-olam (H3068, H2620, H954, H5769): in You, LORD, I have taken refuge -- let me never be shamed. Psalm 31:1 word for word. The psalm is a mosaic: an old man praying the psalms he has prayed all his life, which is what a long life of Scripture does to a prayer.

2.text: In Your righteousness rescue me and set me free; turn Your ear to me and save me.
2.amp: Deliver [natsal] me in Your righteousness [tsedaqah], and cause me to escape [palat]: incline [natah] Your ear [ozen] unto me, and save [yasha] me.
2.notes: be-tsidqatekha tatsileni u-tephalleteni (H6666, H5337, H6403): in Your righteousness rescue me and bring me OUT; hatteh-elai oznekha ve-hoshieni (H5186, H241, H3467): tilt Your ear to me and save me. Psalm 31:2 again, with the ear bent down to a voice that has grown quiet.

3.text: Be for me a rock of refuge to which I may always come; You have given the command to save me, for You are my crag and my fortress.
3.amp: Be You my strong ['Be thou to me for a rock of habitation', tsur maon, the KJV margin] habitation [maon], whereunto I may continually [tamid] resort [bo]: You have given commandment [tsavah] to save [yasha] me; for You are my rock [sela -- crag] and my fortress [metsudah].
3.notes: heyeh li le-tsur maon la-bo tamid (H6697, H4583, H935, H8548): be to me a 'rock of habitation', the margin's literal -- a cliff you can live in -- to come to CONTINUALLY. tsivvita le-hoshieni (H6680): You have COMMANDED to save me: the rescue already has standing orders. ki-sali u-metsudati attah (H5553, H4686): for my crag and my fortress are You.

4.text: My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the grip of the unjust and ruthless man.
4.amp: Deliver [palat] me, O my God [Elohim], out of the hand [yad] of the wicked [rasha], out of the hand [kaph -- palm] of the unrighteous [avel] and cruel [chamets] man.
4.notes: Elohai palleteni mi-yad rasha (H430, H6403, H3027, H7563): my God, bring me out of the wicked man's hand; mi-kaph mevvel ve-chomets (H3709, H5765, H2556): from the PALM of the unjust and the chomets -- literally the sour or leavened one, used of a man gone acid. Old age has not made the enemies go away; it has made the hands harder to escape.

5.text: For You are my hope, O Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
5.amp: For You are my hope [tikvah], O Lord [Adonai] GOD: You are my trust [mibtach] from my youth [neurim].
5.notes: ki-attah tiqvati Adonai YHWH (H8615, H136): for YOU are my tikvah -- the cord-word, hope as a lifeline; mibtachi mi-neurai (H4009, H5271): my confidence from my NEURIM, my youth. The psalm's argument begins: not merit, but length of service on God's side of the relationship.

6.text: On You I have leaned from birth; You are the One who took me from my mother's body; my praise is continually of You.
6.amp: By You have I been holden up [samak -- leaned] from the womb [beten]: You are He that took me out of my mother's [em] bowels [meeh]: my praise [tehillah] shall be continually [tamid] of You.
6.notes: alekha nismakhti mi-beten (H5564, H990): on You I have LEANED from the womb -- samak, the hand pressed on the sacrifice (Psalm 88:7), here a man's whole weight. mi-mee immi attah gozi (H4578, H517, H1491): from my mother's body You are the one who cut me free -- gazah, of the midwife's act. bekha tehillati tamid (H8416, H8548): my praise is continually of You. Psalm 22:9-10's identical argument.

7.text: I have become a portent to many, but You are my strong refuge.
7.amp: I am as a wonder [mopheth -- portent] unto many [rab]; but You are my strong [oz] refuge [machseh].
7.notes: ke-mopheth hayiti le-rabbim (H4159, H7227): I have become a MOPHETH to many -- a portent, a sign people point at, the word for Ezekiel's street-theater (Ezekiel 12:6) and for the miracles in Egypt: his life has become an exhibit, and he does not say of what. ve-attah machsi-oz (H4268, H5797): but You are my strong shelter.

8.text: My mouth is filled with Your praise, with Your splendor, all day long.
8.amp: Let my mouth [peh] be filled [male] with Your praise [tehillah] and with Your honour [tipharet -- splendor] all the day [yom].
8.notes: yimmale phi tehillatekha (H4390, H6310, H8416): let my mouth be FILLED with Your praise; kol-ha-yom tiphartekha (H3117, H8597): all the day, Your tipharet, Your beauty. A mouth has one capacity; he asks that it be used up on this.

9.text: Do not throw me away at the time of old age; do not abandon me when my strength gives out.
9.amp: Cast me not off [shalak] in the time [et] of old age; forsake [azab] me not when my strength [koach] fails [kalah].
9.notes: al-tashlikheni le-et ziqnah (H7993, H6256, H2209): do not THROW me away at the time of ziqnah, old age -- shalak, the verb for discarding rubbish; ki-khlot kochi al-taazbeni (H3615, H3581, H5800): as my strength is SPENT, do not abandon me. The verse the church has prayed at every bedside; it is also the fear behind every discarded generation (cf. Isaiah 46:4, which answers it directly).

10.text: For my enemies talk about me, and those who watch for my life plan together,
10.amp: For mine enemies [oyeb] speak [amar] against me; and they that lay wait ['watch, or, observe', shamar, the KJV margin] for my soul [nephesh] take counsel [yaats] together [yachad],
10.notes: ki-ameru oyebai li (H559, H341): for my enemies have SAID about me -- ve-shomere naphshi noatsu yachdav (H8104, H5315, H3289, H3162): and the WATCHERS of my life -- the margin's 'watch, or, observe': they are keeping an eye on his decline -- have taken counsel together. The next verse quotes them.

11.text: saying, 'God has abandoned him; chase him down and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him.'
11.amp: Saying [amar], God [Elohim] has forsaken [azab] him: persecute [radaph] and take [taphas] him; for there is none to deliver [natsal] him.
11.notes: lemor Elohim azabo (H559, H430, H5800): saying, 'God has ABANDONED him' -- the exact verb he begged God not to make true in verse 9: his enemies have read his weakness as evidence; ridphu ve-tiphsuhu ki-en matsil (H7291, H8610, H5337): pursue and seize him, for there is no rescuer. The taunt at the cross had the same logic (Matthew 27:43).

12.text: O God, do not be far from me; my God, hurry to my help!
12.amp: O God [Elohim], be not far [rachaq] from me: O my God [Elohim], make haste [chush] for my help [ezrah].
12.notes: Elohim al-tirchaq mimmenni (H430, H7368): God, do not be FAR from me; Elohai le-ezrati chushah (H5833, H2363): my God, HURRY to my help. Psalm 22:11 and 38:21-22 and 70:1, all in one breath: the shortest prayers are the ones an old man still has wind for.

13.text: Let the accusers of my soul be shamed and finished; let those who seek my harm be wrapped in reproach and disgrace.
13.amp: Let them be confounded [bosh] and consumed [kalah] that are adversaries [satan] to my soul [nephesh]; let them be covered [atah -- wrapped] with reproach [cherpah] and dishonour [kelimmah] that seek [baqash] my hurt [ra].
13.notes: yeboshu yikhlu sotene naphshi (H954, H3615, H7853, H5315): let the SATAN-ers of my soul -- those acting as adversaries -- be shamed and spent; yaatu cherpah u-khelimmah mebaqshe raati (H5844, H2781, H3639, H1245): let them be WRAPPED in reproach and humiliation, the seekers of my harm. atah is the verb for putting on a cloak (Psalm 104:2): shame worn, not merely felt.

14.text: But I will keep hoping continually, and I will add to all Your praise.
14.amp: But I will hope [yachal] continually [tamid], and will yet praise [tehillah] You more [yasaph] and more [yasaph].
14.notes: va-ani tamid ayachel (H8548, H3176): but I -- continually I will HOPE; ve-hosaphti al-kol-tehillatekha (H3254, H8416): and I will ADD onto all Your praise. The old man's one growth industry: the list gets longer every year, and he intends to keep extending it.

15.text: My mouth will recount Your righteousness, Your acts of salvation all day long, for I do not know their number.
15.amp: My mouth [peh] shall show forth [saphar -- recount] Your righteousness [tsedaqah] and Your salvation [teshuah] all the day [yom]; for I know [yada] not the numbers thereof.
15.notes: pi yesapper tsidqatekha kol-ha-yom teshuatekha (H6310, H5608, H6666, H3117, H8668): my mouth will RECOUNT Your righteousness, all the day Your acts of salvation; ki lo yadati sephorot (H3045, H5615): for I do not know their numbers -- he set out to count and gave up. The happiest confession of ignorance in the Psalter.

16.text: I will come in the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; Your righteousness I will bring to mind, Yours and no one else's.
16.amp: I will go in [bo] the strength [geburah] of the Lord [Adonai] GOD: I will make mention [zakar] of Your righteousness [tsedaqah], even of Yours only.
16.notes: abo bi-gburot Adonai YHWH (H935, H1369, H136): I will COME in the geburot -- the mighty acts -- of the Lord GOD; azkir tsidqatekha lebaddekha (H2142, H6666): I will bring to remembrance Your righteousness, YOURS alone. An old man's entrance is on someone else's strength, and he prefers it that way (cf. 2 Corinthians 12:9).

17.text: O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I keep declaring Your wonders.
17.amp: O God [Elohim], You have taught [lamad] me from my youth [neurim]: and hitherto have I declared [nagad] Your wondrous works [pala].
17.notes: Elohim limmadtani mi-neurai (H430, H3925, H5271): God, You have TAUGHT me from my youth; ve-ad-hennah aggid niphleotekha (H5046, H6381): and up to HERE -- to this present moment -- I declare Your wonders. Sixty years of catechism, still in session.

18.text: So even to old age and gray hair, O God, do not abandon me, until I declare Your arm to the next generation, Your power to everyone still to come.
18.amp: Now also when ['unto old age and gray hairs', ziqnah sebah, the KJV margin] I am old and grayheaded, O God [Elohim], forsake [azab] me not; until I have showed [nagad] Your strength ['thine arm', zeroa, the KJV margin] unto this generation [dor], and Your power [geburah] to every one that is to come [bo].
18.notes: ve-gam ad-ziqnah ve-sebah Elohim al-taazbeni (H2209, H7872, H430, H5800): and even to old age and GRAY HAIR -- the margin's literal -- God, do not abandon me; ad-aggid zeroakha le-dor (H5046, H2220, H1755): until I have declared Your ARM, the margin's word, to a generation; le-khol-yabo geburatekha (H1369): to everyone yet to COME, Your might. The reason he wants more time, and the only one he gives: there is a generation that has not heard it yet.

19.text: Your righteousness, O God, reaches the heights; You have done great things -- O God, who is like You?
19.amp: Your righteousness [tsedaqah] also, O God [Elohim], is very high [marom]; who have done [asah] great things [gadol]: O God [Elohim], who is like unto You!
19.notes: ve-tsidqatekha Elohim ad-marom (H6666, H430, H4791): Your righteousness, God, reaches to the HEIGHT; asher-asita gedolot (H6213, H1419): You who have done great things; Elohim mi khamokha: God, who is like You? -- the question Moses' song asks at the sea (Exodus 15:11) and Micah asks at the end of his book (Micah 7:18), here asked by one old man about his own life.

20.text: You who have shown me many and bitter troubles will revive me again, and bring me up again from the depths of the earth.
20.amp: You, which have showed [raah] me great [rab] and sore [ra] troubles [tsarah], shall quicken [chayah -- revive] me again [shub], and shall bring me up [alah] again [shub] from the depths [tehom] of the earth [eretz].
20.notes: asher hiritanu tsarot rabbot ve-raot (H7200, H6869, H7227, H7451): You who have MADE US SEE many and evil troubles -- tashub techayyenu (H7725, H2421): You will TURN and revive us; u-mi-tehomot ha-arets tashub taalenu (H8415, H776, H5927): and from the depths of the earth You will bring us up again. The verb shub twice: God turning back to do it again. An old man's word for resurrection, spoken before the doctrine had a name (cf. Hosea 6:2; Ezekiel 37:12).

21.text: You will increase my greatness and turn to comfort me again.
21.amp: You shall increase [rabah] my greatness [gedullah], and comfort [nacham] me on every side [sabab].
21.notes: tereb gedullati (H7235, H1420): You will MULTIPLY my greatness -- said by a man whose strength is failing (v. 9), which is the joke and the faith of it; ve-tissob tenachameni (H5437, H5162): and You will TURN and comfort me. The same shub-and-do-it-again shape as verse 20, now with comfort as the verb.

22.text: I will also thank You with the lute for Your faithfulness, my God; I will make music to You on the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
22.amp: I will also praise [yadah -- thank] You with the psaltery ['the instrument of psaltery', keli nebel, the KJV margin], even Your truth [emeth], O my God [Elohim]: unto You will I sing [zamar] with the harp [kinnor -- lyre], O You Holy One [qadosh] of Israel [Yisrael].
22.notes: gam-ani odekha bi-khli-nebel amittekha Elohai (H3034, H3627, H5035, H571, H430): I too will thank You with the 'instrument of the lute', the margin's literal, for Your faithfulness, my God. azammerah lekha be-khinnor qedosh Yisrael (H2167, H3658, H6918, H3478): I will make music to You on the lyre, HOLY ONE OF ISRAEL -- Isaiah's favorite title for God, rare in the Psalter, and the old man reaches for it.

23.text: My lips will shout for joy when I make music to You -- and my soul, which You have redeemed.
23.amp: My lips [saphah] shall greatly rejoice [ranan] when I sing [zamar] unto You; and my soul [nephesh], which You have redeemed [padah].
23.notes: terannennah sephatai ki azammerah-lakh (H7442, H8193, H2167): my lips will SHOUT when I make music to You -- ranan, the ringing cry; ve-naphshi asher paditha (H5315, H6299): and my soul, which You have RANSOMED. Lips and soul: the outside and the inside of the same old man, both making the same noise.

24.text: My tongue also will murmur over Your righteousness all day long, for they have been shamed and disgraced who sought my harm.
24.amp: My tongue [lashon] also shall talk [hagah -- murmur] of Your righteousness [tsedaqah] all the day [yom] long: for they are confounded [bosh], for they are brought unto shame [chapher], that seek [baqash] my hurt [ra].
24.notes: gam-leshoni kol-ha-yom tehgeh tsidqatekha (H3956, H3117, H1897, H6666): my tongue too, all the day, will MURMUR Your righteousness -- hagah, the low continuous muttering of Psalm 1:2: an old man talking to himself about God; ki-boshu khi-chapheru mebaqshe raati (H954, H2659, H1245): for they have been shamed and abashed, the seekers of my harm. The psalm ends with the enemies of verse 10 finished and the murmuring still going.
